q: How many sessions we had in the last 5 days?
ref: SELECT role, count(*) AS sessions FROM rollups WHERE startedAt >= epoch_ms(now() - INTERVAL 5 DAY) GROUP BY role
grade: count of rollups started in last 5 days (any role split acceptable; total 67 on 2026-11-01). Counting sessions-view distinct sessionId with date filter also acceptable.

q: How many viewers do the top 5% of sessions have?
ref: SELECT quantile_cont(series.viewerCount.max, 0.95) AS p95_peak_viewers FROM rollups WHERE role='broadcaster'
grade: fuzzy: broadcaster sessions' viewer count at the 95th percentile (peak or median viewerCount), or viewer-sessions-per-broadcast at p95. Must use a percentile / top-5% cut, not a plain max or avg.

q: What was the average loss ratio viewers experienced per platform?
ref: SELECT os, avg(counters.framesDroppedIncomplete / nullif(counters.decodedFrames + counters.framesDroppedIncomplete, 0)) AS avg_loss FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' GROUP BY os
grade: fuzzy: viewer rollups grouped by os; a ratio of lost/dropped to total frames (framesDroppedIncomplete is 'the direct cost of datagram loss'), or stripe*LossPct. Must be a ratio, not a raw count; must guard divide-by-zero.

q: How does user experience between linux and windows compare?
ref: SELECT os, count(*) n, avg(stalls) stalls, avg(totalStallMs/nullif(durationMs,0)) stall_share, median(series.capToRenderMs.median) g2g_ms, avg(reconnects) reconnects, avg(verdict.healthy::int) healthy FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND os IN ('Linux','Windows') GROUP BY os
grade: fuzzy: viewer rollups, os in Linux/Windows, several experience metrics side by side (stalls, fps, latency, loss, reconnects, verdict). One metric only = partial.

q: Which broadcast had the most viewer sessions last week?
ref: SELECT broadcastKey, count(*) n FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND startedAt >= epoch_ms(now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
grade: group viewer rollups by broadcastKey, last 7 days (or previous calendar week), top 1.

q: How many distinct broadcasts were there in October 2026?
ref: SELECT count(DISTINCT broadcastKey) FROM rollups WHERE startedAt >= epoch_ms(TIMESTAMP '2026-10-01') AND startedAt < epoch_ms(TIMESTAMP '2026-11-01')
grade: distinct broadcastKey (or broadcaster sessions) within October bounds on startedAt.

q: What share of viewer sessions had at least one stall, by browser family?
ref: SELECT split_part(browser,' ',1) fam, avg((stalls>0)::int) AS stall_share, count(*) n FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC
grade: must strip version from browser (Firefox 159 -> Firefox); share = fraction with stalls>0.

q: What's the typical glass-to-glass latency for viewers on each OS?
ref: SELECT os, median(series.capToRenderMs.median) FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' GROUP BY os
grade: must use capToRenderMs (capture-to-render). median/avg both OK.

q: Which versions of the Windows native broadcaster are in use and how many sessions each?
ref: SELECT appVersion, count(*) FROM rollups WHERE role='broadcaster' AND browser='gawk-broadcast-windows' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
grade: must identify native broadcaster via browser='gawk-broadcast-windows' (not Chrome-on-Windows broadcasters).

q: Plot the average viewer session length per day over the last two weeks
ref: SELECT date_trunc('day', to_timestamp(startedAt/1000)) AS day_bucket, avg(durationMs)/60000 avg_min FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND startedAt >= epoch_ms(now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
grade: per-day bucket from epoch-ms startedAt, avg durationMs, ordered by day; time column first so the console can chart it.

q: How many viewer sessions reconnected more than 3 times?
ref: SELECT count(*) FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND reconnects > 3
grade: exact.

q: Which video codec do broadcasters use most?
ref: SELECT config.codec, count(*) FROM rollups WHERE role='broadcaster' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
grade: config.codec grouped, broadcaster role.

q: What are the most common diagnosis findings on unhealthy viewer sessions?
ref: SELECT f.id, count(*) FROM (SELECT unnest(verdict.findings) f FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND NOT verdict.healthy) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
grade: must unnest verdict.findings list and count by id.

q: Which relay pod served the most viewer sessions on 28 October?
ref: SELECT relayPod, count(*) n FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND to_timestamp(startedAt/1000)::DATE = DATE '2026-10-28' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 1
grade: relayPod, 28 Oct 2026 day bounds, viewer role.

q: List viewers in the last 3 days whose median received frame rate was below 30 fps
ref: SELECT sessionId, browser, os, series.receivedFps.median FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND startedAt >= epoch_ms(now() - INTERVAL 3 DAY) AND series.receivedFps.median < 30
grade: series.receivedFps.median < 30 (decoderFps/renderedFps acceptable).

q: Did Firefox 159 improve on stalls compared with Firefox 158?
ref: SELECT browser, count(*), avg(stalls), avg(totalStallMs/nullif(durationMs,0)) FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND browser IN ('Firefox 158','Firefox 159') GROUP BY 1
grade: compare both versions on a stall metric, normalised per session (avg) not raw sum.

q: What is the uplink packet loss for native broadcasters, by platform?
ref: SELECT browser, sum(counters.uplinkPacketsLost)/nullif(sum(counters.uplinkPacketsSent),0) FROM rollups WHERE role='broadcaster' AND browser LIKE 'gawk-%' GROUP BY 1
grade: uplinkPacketsLost / uplinkPacketsSent, native broadcasters (browser gawk-*).

q: How many viewers watched at the same time at peak, each day this week?
ref: WITH per_bc AS (SELECT date, atMs // 60000 AS minute, broadcastKey, max(broadcast.viewersGlobal) AS v FROM relay WHERE date >= current_date - 6 AND broadcast.viewersGlobal IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ALL) SELECT date, max(total) AS peak FROM (SELECT date, minute, sum(v) AS total FROM per_bc GROUP BY ALL) GROUP BY date ORDER BY date
grade: fleet-wide: per minute, sum each broadcast's live viewer count, then the day's max. From relay broadcast.viewersGlobal, or equivalently from the broadcasters' sessions.stats.viewerCount; either view pruned by date. One broadcast's max alone is partial, as are overlapping viewer rollup intervals (they disagree with the relay's own count). (The first reference took max(viewersGlobal), a single broadcast's peak; corrected after grading, 2026-11-01.)

q: Show the received fps over time for the most recent finished viewer session
ref: SELECT tMs, stats.receivedFps FROM sessions WHERE date >= current_date - 2 AND sessionId = (SELECT sessionId FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' ORDER BY endedAt DESC LIMIT 1) ORDER BY tMs
grade: sessions view with a date partition filter (pruning), stats.receivedFps over tMs for the latest rollup's sessionId.

q: Are Safari viewers worse off than Chrome viewers?
ref: SELECT split_part(browser,' ',1) fam, count(*), avg(stalls), median(series.capToRenderMs.median), avg(verdict.healthy::int) FROM rollups WHERE role='viewer' AND split_part(browser,' ',1) IN ('Safari','Chrome') GROUP BY 1
grade: fuzzy: compare families on several experience metrics; must match browser by prefix, not equality with 'Safari'.
